clue.text: Verify angry European broadcast

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A news item tells listeners to confirm the story of an irate continental who went on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-check a fact against another source is to verify it.

clue.text: Man of the church is correct to ignore bill

indicators.note: ignoring the bill means leaving its letters out

parts.note: accurate means correct
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A clergyman is right to skip paying a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is a clergyman assisting a parish priest, a man of the church.

clue.text: Appoint minister by name after radio broadcast

indicators.note: after puts the name's letter following the scrambled radio
broadcast also means scattered about, like seed, so the letters are spread out anew

explanation.surface: A politician is named after a radio announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks political; here it is a member of the clergy, and appointing one is a church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to make someone a priest or minister by a church rite.

clue.text: Important case developed about university is a bit of an exaggeration

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the university
the letters have developed into a new form, an anagram

explanation.surface: A major legal case unfolding at a university is somewhat overblown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a great fuss over something trivial, which is overstating its importance.

clue.text: Carers from hospital composed poems about Hades mostly

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap round the underworld
composed means put together, so the letters are arranged in a new order
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Hades is the underworld, hell

explanation.surface: Hospital staff wrote verses about the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: POEMS is rearranged into OMEPS, which goes 'about' HEL ('mostly' drops the final L of HELL). Home helps are British domestic carers who visit the elderly or sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Home helps are people employed to look after the housebound in their homes, a kind of carer.

clue.text: Parliament vacated after scream in vault

indicators.note: after puts the emptied Parliament behind the cry

parts.note: a scream is a cry

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of Parliament remain

explanation.surface: MPs left the chamber after a scream from the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vault, usually beneath a church.

clue.text: Volunteers needed in case of shooting party

indicators.note: the volunteers are needed inside the other letters, so they are placed within them
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A shooting party needs volunteers to come along as beaters.
explanation.walkthrough: TA stands for the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve. 'Shooting party' looks like one phrase but 'party' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a men-only celebration before a wedding, so stag alone names that kind of party.

clue.text: Origin of this personal transport for urban area

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: own means personal, as in 'my own car'
to ship is to transport

explanation.surface: The source of this private vehicle is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a town or settlement, a built-up district.

clue.text: Generally gutted sailor must be spinning

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: a rating is a naval sailor without a commission

explanation.surface: A sailor who is broadly disappointed must be in a whirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' reads as British slang for bitterly disappointed, but it empties 'Generally' to GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrating means rotating or whirling around, spinning.

clue.text: Beer goes on board ship after permission for trade events

indicators.note: after puts the ship with its cargo behind the permission

parts.note: clearance is official permission

indicators.note: going on board a vessel means going inside it

parts.note: SS is steamship
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Beer is loaded onto a vessel once customs give the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance sales are shop events selling off stock cheaply, a kind of trading occasion.

clue.text: Show lover must have change of heart

indicators.note: the heart, or central letter, of the lover is swapped for a different letter

parts.note: Romeo is the archetypal lover, from Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A display of devotion requires a lover to reconsider his feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle letter M of ROMEO for D.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public show of cowboy skills like bronco riding and roping.

clue.text: Ship that might bear fruit?

parts.note: the Pilgrim Fathers' vessel of 1620 is named after the hawthorn's spring blossom, and blossom goes on to produce fruit

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a vessel that could grow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the ship's name as two words: a bloom of May, which as a blossom might in time bear fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous ship that carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620; its name also describes a spring blossom.

clue.text: President with hotel must accept one notable success

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the president's name takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: Donald Trump, a US President
I is the Roman numeral for one
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A politician staying at a hotel must welcome a celebrated achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral goes in after the second letter of the president's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement, a striking success.

clue.text: Poles covered by characteristic passage

indicators.note: the poles sit inside, wrapped by the letters of the characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people hidden by some feature of a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; here it is the compass poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage or conveyance from one place to another.

clue.text: A couple of million swallowed by rising prices may be a cause of pain

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so the pair goes within the other word

parts.note: inflation is a general rise in prices
M is million, so a couple of them is two Ms

explanation.surface: An economic warning that soaring costs eating up millions will hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Swelling and redness of tissue brings soreness, so it is something that can cause pain.

clue.text: Type of purchase made by man reportedly having class

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a man is male
an order is a class or rank, as in biology

explanation.surface: Buying something from a man said to have style.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is buying goods by post from a catalogue, a way of shopping.

clue.text: Staff ego unfortunately not visible to the audience

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An actor's inflated sense of self, sadly hidden from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage means in the wings, out of view of those watching the play.

clue.text: A daughter may be in list for such a car

indicators.note: may be in places the pair inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of names, a rota

explanation.surface: A daughter could appear on a register for a certain vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater sports car.

clue.text: Illustration that could be precise, if not funny

indicators.note: funny in the sense of odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged into something strange

explanation.surface: A picture that is accurate even if it lacks humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if not funny' reads as a qualification of 'precise', but 'funny' signals that PRECISE IF NOT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontispiece is the illustration facing a book's title page.

clue.text: Engineers currently unknown may find fame

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
now means currently, at present
N is an unknown quantity in mathematics

explanation.surface: Engineers who are presently obscure might become celebrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is celebrity or wide acclaim, the same as fame.

clue.text: Precursor of some peripheral devices

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The forerunner of certain computer add-ons such as printers.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald announces what is coming, so it is a forerunner or precursor.

clue.text: Profile Royal Marines by answer and weapon

parts.note: a profile is a side view
RM abbreviates the Royal Marines, Britain's naval infantry

explanation.surface: A sketch of Royal Marines set beside a reply and a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a weapon carried at the side, such as a pistol or bayonet.

clue.text: Communication channels raising target to incorporate education

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take in, so the reversed word holds the education
in a down clue raising means lifting from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an aim is a target

explanation.surface: Television and radio lift their sights to include learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns AIM into MIA, since in a down answer a raised word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the press, radio and television, the means of mass communication.

clue.text: Repugnant prospect offered to old boy

indicators.note: the view is handed over to follow the former pupil

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a prospect is a view, or scene

explanation.surface: A former pupil is presented with a distasteful outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene things are offensive and disgusting, so they are repugnant.

clue.text: Amazed — area seemed to protect them initially

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the letters of 'seemed' enclose the initial

parts.note: sounded means seemed, as in 'it sounded right'

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word them

explanation.surface: Astonished at how a region appeared to guard some people.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the first letter of 'them', goes inside SOUNDED, after its S, and A for 'area' goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be astounded is to be shocked with surprise, that is, amazed.

clue.text: Sponge pudding from the east with filling of jam

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit purée and cream

indicators.note: the filling is the centre, the middle letter of jam

explanation.surface: A sponge pudding from Asia with jam inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge pudding' reads as one dessert, but 'Sponge' is the definition and 'pudding' gives FOOL. A fool is a British dessert of fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous fruit of a gourd used as a bath sponge.

clue.text: Bring in listener before end of bulletin

indicators.note: before places the listener's letters ahead of the final one

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of bulletin

explanation.surface: Invite an audience member in ahead of the news finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to bring it in as income.

clue.text: Stationed last of troops in turbulent Rio Grande

indicators.note: in puts the final letter inside the stirred river letters
turbulent water is churned up, so the river's letters are stirred about
last of picks the final letter of troops

explanation.surface: A soldier posted on a wild stretch of the river at the US border.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the last letter of 'troops', goes 'in' GARRIONED, the anagram of RIO GRANDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops garrisoned in a town are posted or stationed there.
